hints: Notice the bob is stationary, so the vertical forces must balance and the horizontal forces must balance separately.
Resolve the tension $T$ which acts at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical into a vertical part and a horizontal part using $\cos$ and $\sin$.
Match the downward weight $W$ to the upward vertical part of $T$ and match $H$ to the sideways part of $T$ to pick the correct equation.
walkthrough: The bob is in equilibrium, so resultant force is zero. Vertically, upward force must equal downward $W$, and horizontally, leftward force must equal rightward $H$.
Tension $T$ acts along the string at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical. Its component along the vertical is adjacent to the $30^{\circ}$ angle, so it is $T \cos 30^{\circ}$ upward.
Its component perpendicular to the vertical is opposite the $30^{\circ}$ angle, so the horizontal component is $T \sin 30^{\circ}$ to the left.
Set components equal for equilibrium: vertically $W = T \cos 30^{\circ}$ and horizontally $H = T \sin 30^{\circ}$.
Comparing with the statements, $W = T \cos 30^{\circ}$ matches the vertical balance. This is option D.

options.A: The horizontal force $H$ balances the horizontal component of $T$, which is $T \sin 30^{\circ}$, not $T \cos 30^{\circ}$.
options.B: Resolving horizontally gives $H = T \sin 30^{\circ}$, so $T = H / \sin 30^{\circ}$, not $H \sin 30^{\circ}$.
options.C: The weight $W$ balances the vertical component of $T$, which uses $\cos 30^{\circ}$ because the $30^{\circ}$ angle is to the vertical.
options.D: Vertical equilibrium requires $W$ to equal the vertical component $T \cos 30^{\circ}$.
